Summary: FR-3- The system shall allow authenticated customers to update their phone number through the customer portal.
Description: Business capability: Enable authenticated customers to update their phone number through the existing self-service portal. Customer value: Customers can maintain accurate contact information without Customer Support intervention. Expected outcome: A valid phone-number change is securely processed, reflected in the customer profile, recorded in the audit history, and available through request status. Assumptions: The customer is authenticated; an existing customer profile is available; existing customer data services support profile updates. Architecture considerations: Reuse the existing portal, Identity Provider, API Gateway, Customer Profile Service, Profile Data Store, audit logging, and cloud platform. Protect PII, enforce tenant isolation and authorization, apply required-field and format validation, consider whether ownership verification or step-up authentication is required, and meet reliability, performance, availability, and privacy requirements.

Summary: FR-5 - The system shall validate all required fields before accepting a request.
Description: Business capability: Validate required profile fields before a customer update request is accepted for processing. Customer value: Customers receive immediate feedback and avoid submitting incomplete requests that would fail later. Expected outcome: Incomplete or invalid submissions are rejected without changing stored profile data, while valid submissions can proceed to processing. Assumptions: Required fields and validation rules are defined for mailing address, email address, and phone number. Architecture considerations: Apply consistent validation across the portal and Customer Profile Service, with the service remaining authoritative. Protect PII in validation responses and telemetry, maintain two-second response objectives under normal conditions, support horizontal scaling, and ensure validation behavior is tenant-aware and does not affect existing profile viewing.

Summary: FR-7 - The system shall display validation errors to the customer with instructions on how to resolve
Description: Business capability: Present actionable validation errors when submitted profile information cannot be accepted. Customer value: Customers can understand and correct problems without contacting Customer Support. Expected outcome: The portal identifies the affected field, explains the issue in meaningful language, and provides guidance for correction without exposing sensitive technical information. Assumptions: Validation services return usable error categories or codes that can be translated into customer-facing guidance. Architecture considerations: Coordinate portal and service validation responses, support address-correction candidates where applicable, meet accessibility requirements, avoid exposing PII or internal system details, preserve correlation information for support, and maintain responsive behavior under normal operating conditions.

Summary: FR-9 - The system shall update the customer profile after successful processing.
Description: Business capability: Persist successfully processed mailing-address, email-address, and phone-number changes to the customer profile. Customer value: Customers see accurate current profile information after a completed request. Expected outcome: Authorized changes are stored consistently, do not overwrite newer updates, and become available through existing profile-viewing functionality. Assumptions: The Customer Profile Service and Profile Data Store support updates and appropriate concurrency controls; authoritative ownership of each profile field is confirmed. Architecture considerations: Enforce identity and tenant authorization, protect PII in transit and at rest, use concurrency controls to prevent lost updates, maintain consistency with audit and status outcomes, support reliable recovery from partial failure, and avoid degrading existing profile APIs.

Summary: FR-10 - The system shall return processing status to the customer.
Description: Business capability: Provide customer-visible status for an accepted profile-update request. Customer value: Customers understand whether their request is processing, completed, or failed without contacting Customer Support. Expected outcome: The portal uses the request identifier to retrieve and display a current, tenant-scoped processing status and final outcome. Assumptions: Accepted requests are assigned a durable request identifier and the Customer Profile Service can maintain request state. Architecture considerations: Reuse the portal, API Gateway, and profile service status capability; enforce authorization and tenant isolation; meet response-time and availability targets; protect PII; retain failed requests for investigation; and ensure status remains accurate during retries, recovery, and staged rollout.

Summary: FR-8 - The system shall submit valid requests to an automated workflow for processing.
Description:
Description

Business capability: Accept a valid profile-update request and submit it to an automated workflow for reliable processing. Customer value: Profile changes can be completed quickly and consistently without manual Customer Support activity. Expected outcome: Each accepted request receives a request identifier, is durably recorded, enters Processing status, and proceeds to a safe terminal outcome without being lost. Assumptions: The existing Customer Profile Service can be extended to support orchestration and durable request status, or an architecture decision will identify an alternative. Architecture considerations: Reuse the API Gateway and Customer Profile Service where practical; support asynchronous processing, idempotency, bounded retry, correlation identifiers, tenant isolation, horizontal scaling, multi-availability-zone deployment, observability, and recovery of failed requests.
